principles: Core modules must not import handler shells.
Gate and signature behavior must have a single source of truth.
Refactor scope stays limited to relocation and import rewiring.
Verification must prove both layering and unchanged INIT_CHECK gate behavior.
drivers: State-machine gate code consumes init-check primitives during INIT to INIT_CHECK transitions.
Existing handler command still owns writing init-check.json and should keep its outward behavior.
The story has gate/state-machine risk, so false pass or semantic drift is higher cost than a small compatibility re-export.

options.name: extract-core-module
pros: Removes the core-to-handler import with minimal scope.
Matches the existing delivery-check-hash extraction pattern.
Lets handler and machine share one implementation.
cons: Requires careful import and export rewiring.
May leave command-owner registry strings in handlers, which needs explicit reasoning.

options.name: duplicate-core-helpers
pros: Fast mechanical way to remove the import.
cons: Creates two implementations of the signature/gate algorithm.

options.name: move-entire-handler-to-core
cons: Too broad for a refactor backlog story.
Would mix command shell concerns and metadata locking into core.

rationale: Create a core init-check gate/hash module, import it from machine and handler, and keep handler as the command shell. This removes the layer violation while preserving one algorithm and existing command ownership.

preMortem.scenario: Hash algorithm changes accidentally during relocation.
preMortem.trigger: The extracted code alters normalized checklist/background inputs or salt usage.
preMortem.consequence: Valid init-check evidence could be rejected or tampered evidence accepted.
preMortem.mitigation: Move code mechanically, run init-check bootstrap and worktree-authority smoke tests, and keep comments/signature domain intact.

preMortem.trigger: Agent matching or agentResults fallback changes while extracting helper functions.
preMortem.consequence: A story could pass INIT_CHECK without product-reviewer or koala-review-story-init evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Run targeted init-check required-agent coverage through init-check bootstrap/worktree authority tests and record explicit evidence.

preMortem.scenario: Layering violation appears fixed but another core import still references handlers/init-check.
preMortem.trigger: Only machine.ts import is updated while another core file or generated path keeps the same dependency.
preMortem.consequence: The architectural defect remains hidden behind a passing build.
preMortem.mitigation: Record grep evidence that core has no import from handlers/init-check after implementation.
